To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most common pesticides in agriculture, such as pyrethroids, organophosphates and neonicotinoids, are toxic to honey bees, and the risk of their use depends mainly on the dose and time of exposure.

the impacts of pesticides on honey bee colonies depend on the dose and the time that bees are exposed, and that the impacts of these chemicals can be avoided by using pesticides that are less toxic to bees and by applying them in a manner that minimizes the exposure of bees.

(1) the most common way of exposure of bees is through ingestion of pesticide residues found in the nectar and pollen of the plants; (2) honey bees are also exposed by contact with treated plants, and through inhalation of pesticide vapour; (3) pesticides may cause acute and chronic toxicity, and sublethal effects, which may reduce colony performance; (4) the severity of the toxicity is determined by the dose and the time that the bees are exposed to the pesticide;
